headline: Interpretable deep models map brain age and metabolic biomarkers in aging and dementia
label: Neuroimaging Brain Age Biomarkers
summary: Recent preprints apply explainable, self-supervised and surface-based models to regional brain biomarkers in Alzheimer's, dementia, and development.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of learned representations to derive interpretable, regionally resolved biomarkers from brain imaging. R-NCE, a self-supervised framework, integrates FreeSurfer features from structural MRI and includes brain age gap GWAS analysis in Alzheimer's disease, framed as a cautionary case for imaging biomarkers. A semi-supervised VAE with similarity regularization aligns one latent dimension with cognition in ADNI PET scans, revealing interpretable glucose-metabolism patterns linked to dementia. SurfAge-Net applies a spherical surface-based network with spatial-channel mixing and lateralization-aware attention to predict fine-grained regional brain age. A regional development index in youth identifies three functional connectivity maturation subtypes that are linked to cognition and replicated in HCP-D. What is new is the emphasis on anatomically or cognitively anchored outputs in place of single global scalar predictions.
